steps:
Create the file .github/workflows/publish.yml by running exactly this shell command:

cat > .github/workflows/publish.yml << EOF
name: Upload Python Package

on:
  release:
    types: [created]

jobs:
  deploy:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v2
      with:
        python-version: '3.x'
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install poetry
    - name: Build and publish
      env:
        PYPI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}
      run: |
        poetry publish --build
EOF
expected: The heredoc command completes promptly and .github/workflows/publish.yml is written with the YAML content.
defect: The shell tool stalls on the `cat > file << EOF ... EOF` command and never returns a result ("This got stuck").
Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/gptme/gptme/pull/335 (commit 6a1246f5a2a5b4e0b2376c947e02f32daf5fbfc9). In the 2023 shell tool, ShellSession._run wrote the command to the persistent bash process as a single line `f"{command}; echo ReturnCode:$? {self.delimiter}\n"`. For a heredoc the terminator line `EOF` was therefore followed by `; echo ReturnCode:...` on the same line, so bash never saw a bare `EOF` line, kept reading the heredoc body, never printed the return-code/delimiter marker, and the reader loop blocked forever. PR #335 ('fix: support heredoc/EOF syntax in shell tool', for the duplicate #108) writes the command and the `echo ReturnCode:$? <delimiter>` marker on separate lines and only returns when the marker line is read. The fix first ships in v0.25.0; the pinned revision (v0.35.1) contains it, so the stall is not expected to reproduce there.
